title: Philadelphia Fed Q4 2026 Price and Inflation Expectations Survey (PIES) — 10:00 a.m. ET, the Third District's only quantitative price series, buried under PCE and GDP on the day before Thanksgiving
source: EST: philadelphiafed.org/surveys-and-data/regional-economic-analysis/price-and-inflation-expectations-survey — the SURVEY'S OWN landing page, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 141,301 bytes), whose Release Calendar panel reads verbatim 'Nov 25 2026 | Fourth Quarter 2026 Price and Inflation Expectations Survey | 10:00 a.m.' This discharges the proposal's task (a): the date is now read from a page dedicated to THIS survey, not from the shared calendar row the proposal cited. Corroborated three further ways, all fetched direct 2026-09-09. (1) The bank's calendar endpoint embeds the full 2026 PIES schedule as structured data — Feb 25, May 27, Aug 26, Nov 25, every one at 10:00 a.m. (the `?release=` query string is CLIENT-SIDE: the MBOS-filtered and PIES-filtered URLs return byte-identical 131,096-byte bodies carrying all 237 rows of the year). (2) A construction rule, 4 for 4: PIES is compiled from responses collected inside the monthly MBOS and NBOS, and every 2026 edition publishes the CALENDAR DAY AFTER that quarter's NBOS — NBOS Feb 24 -> PIES Feb 25, May 26 -> May 27, Aug 25 -> Aug 26, Nov 24 -> Nov 25. (3) The published data file itself, /-/media/FRBP/Assets/Surveys-And-Data/PIES/pies-data.xlsx (HTTP 200, 25,050 bytes), whose Notes sheet reads 'Released: August 26, 2026' — matching the calendar's Q3 row exactly, and whose internal build path is X:\RegionalSurveys\MonthlySurveys\monthly_processing\combined\pies\2026_08\webrelease\, confirming both the last edition and the MBOS/NBOS-combined construction. Filed estimate on the same two counts every sibling Third District entry records, NEITHER of which is doubt about the date: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no member for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule (FED: covers the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar only), and this lane does not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL entry written 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, which read the one proposal that existed for this id (proposals/philly-fed-price-inflation-expectations-q4-2026-11-25.from-philly-fed-mfg-2026-12-17.json, filed 2026-09-09) and discharged BOTH tasks it assigned. (a) The date and the 10:00 a.m. time are now read from the survey's own landing page rather than the shared calendar row — see `source`. (b) What the survey publishes is now established rather than unknown: PIES is a quarterly survey of Third District firms (Delaware, southern New Jersey, eastern and central Pennsylvania) asking four point-estimate questions — expected change in the firm's OWN prices over the next four quarters, expected compensation per employee, expected US inflation over the next four quarters, and expected 10-year average US inflation — plus, since mid-2019, the realized change in the firm's own prices over the PAST four quarters. Mean and median are published for all firms and split manufacturing/nonmanufacturing; the series runs 44 quarters, 2015Q4 through 2026Q3. THE PROPOSAL'S CENTRAL CLAIM IS REFUTED, MEASURED. It filed this event because PIES 'is the instrument that would carry forward information the MBOS structurally cannot.' Scored on the publisher's own file against realized district own-price change at the survey's own four-quarter horizon, leave-one-out cross-validated over n=29: PIES expectation used raw MAE 1.103, MBOS prices-paid diffusion fitted MAE 1.107, PIES fitted 1.202, persistence 1.559. PIES and the MBOS are a DEAD HEAT; the expectations survey does not beat the diffusion index it was proposed as an upgrade on. What PIES uniquely supplies is the RULER, not the lead — it is the only Third District price series denominated in percent, and the MBOS diffusion index only becomes a percent by regressing it on PIES history nobody would have without PIES. Impact LOW and symbols [] on grounds this ledger measures rather than assumes: 2026-11-25 08:30 ET already carries pce-2026-11-25 (high, confirmed) and gdp-q3-2026-second-2026-11-25 (high, confirmed), with durable-goods (medium) alongside and beige-book (medium, confirmed) at 14:30 — a sub-state quarterly survey releasing 90 minutes after the Fed's preferred inflation gauge has no identifiable tape of its own, the exact inverse of the philly-fed-mfg-2026-12-17 morning where this bank's survey stands alone. What earns the row is a READING RULE, not a trade: the survey's 10-year US inflation MEAN has been >= 5.4% for 23 consecutive quarters (2021Q1 through 2026Q3, latest 7.3%) while its MEDIAN has never once left the 3.0-4.0 band (latest 3.0). The mean is a fat-right-tail artifact and a headline built on it would be false in effect on the same morning PCE prints. This is an ESTIMATE — it widens caution, licenses nothing, and the ledger's stance is a permanent stand-aside.
